title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building an explicit, highly symmetric combinatorial model of the fundamental groupoid of Σ* = P^1_C minus J = {0,1,∞}, together with its real structure. Σ is the Riemann sphere and Σ_R its real circle. Σ̃ is the real oriented blow-up of Σ at the three points of J: a sphere with three holes, whose boundary circles U_i are the circles of tangent directions at i. This page fixes the combinatorial data in a way equivariant under two symmetries. The first is G_J = Aut(J) ≅ S_3, acting by the real Möbius transformations that permute 0, 1, ∞. The second is complex conjugation τ.

(i) Index sets. The set ω of the two cyclic orders on J is identified with the set of orientations of Σ_R. Once an orientation of Σ is fixed, ω is in bijection with ε = π_0(Σ \ Σ_R), the set of the two hemispheres (a hemisphere induces a boundary orientation on Σ_R). From here on ω and ε are identified; this is why later formulas use ω and ε interchangeably.

Margin NB: the set Rep(J) of frames (orderings (i,j,k)) satisfies Rep(J) ≅ J × ω, via (i,j,k) ↦ (i, cyclic orientation of ijk). This is the S_3-torsor of the 6 orderings.

(ii) Base points, recalled from p.49:
- Q_i: the point of Σ_R antipodal to R_i, i.e. a midpoint of the real segment that does not contain i.
- R_i^ω: the two real tangent directions on U_i.
- P_ε: the poles of the two hemispheres.
- S_i^ε: the tangent directions on U_i pointing into the hemisphere ε.

(iii) Paths (21), counts written above:
- a_i^{ω,ε} (12 = 3·2·2): quarter-turn arcs on the boundary circle U_i from S_i^ε to R_i^ω (23). The transcription's '(quand du tour)' is almost certainly '(quart de tour)'.
- b_i^ω (6): real paths from Q_i along the real segment in direction ω, ending at the tangential point of the puncture reached (24). They lie on Σ̃_R = Dec(Σ_R, J), the real circle cut at J, i.e. three closed segments.
- c_i^ε (6): great-circle arcs from the pole P^ε to Q_i (25).
- d_i^ε (6): great-circle arcs from P^ε to the tangential point S_i^ε (26).
- b̃_i^ω = b_i^ω (b_i^{ω'})^{-1} (27): the full real segment from one puncture to the next.

(iv) Symmetries. Each 6-element packet b, c, d is a G_J-torsor, with g(x_i^ω) = x_{g(i)}^{g(ω)}. Odd permutations lie in PGL_2(R) with negative determinant: they reverse the orientation of Σ_R and swap the hemispheres, so the identification ω = ε is G_J-equivariant. The 12-element packet a is a torsor under Γ = G_J × {1,τ}. By (22), τ fixes ω and b and flips ε on a, c, d.

Purpose (next page). The paths cut Σ̃ into five maximal simply connected open sets: the two hemispherical regions centred at P_ε and three regions centred at Q_i. Their fundamental groups 'based at a simply connected set', Π_ε and Π_i, are linked by transitivity isomorphisms. The whole page is a G_J × Gal(C/R)-equivariant presentation of the fundamental groupoid of P^1 \ {0,1,∞} with tangential and real base points. This is the base-point skeleton needed to write the Galois action on the genus-0 Teichmüller 'lego' (the elements later called f, the S_3 symmetry relations, and complex conjugation).
errors: The final sentence says the endpoints of c_i^ω and d_i^ω are not in Σ* but in ∂Σ̃ \ Σ*. This is false for c_i, whose endpoint Q_i lies in Σ*. It is true for d_i (endpoint S_i on U_i) and for b_i (endpoint R on U_i). Probably a slip for 'b_i, d_i', or the transcription misreads the letters.
Indexing is inconsistent: (21) and (22) write c_i^ε, d_i^ε while (25) and (26) write c_i^ω, d_i^ω. This is harmless only after the identification ω = ε made at the top of the page.

In (27) the source point 'R_{ωi}' lacks its superscript. It should be the tangential point at the opposite end of the segment, R^{ω}_{ω'i} or similar. The orientation conventions for ω versus ω' in (24) and (27) are not fully pinned down on the page.

The claim that the c and d packets are G_J-torsors needs the G_J-action to be by the real Möbius maps, with odd elements exchanging hemispheres. This is correct but implicit. On c and d, τ acts through the same orbit as the transposition fixing i, so these packets are not Γ-torsors. Grothendieck correctly reserves Γ-torsoriality for the a-packet.

ideas.what: Real oriented blow-up of P^1 at {0,1,∞}: a sphere with three boundary circles, used as a model with tangential base points on the boundary
ideas.modern_name: Kato–Nakayama / real oriented blow-up; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; Kato–Nakayama for the log version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) speaks of base points at infinity and the Teichmüller tower but gives no such explicit construction

ideas.what: Base points and paths chosen equivariantly under S_3 × Gal(C/R): real segments, hemisphere poles, quarter-turn arcs on boundary circles
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric set of rational/tangential base points; the S_3 symmetries behind the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT; complex conjugation fixing real paths
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the S_3 and real-structure aspects only qualitatively

ideas.what: Identification of cyclic orders of J with orientations of Σ_R and with hemispheres; frames Rep(J) ≅ J × {cyclic orders}
Packets of paths as torsors under G_J or Γ = G_J × ⟨τ⟩
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant groupoid presentations; orbifold fundamental group of the quotient by S_3 × Z/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. work on the M_{0,4}/S_3 orbifold

missed.claim: This is a fully explicit, Gal(C/R) × S_3-equivariant tangential-base-point groupoid for P^1 \ {0,1,∞}: 12 quarter-turn arcs plus three 6-element packets of real and great-circle arcs. It is a careful precursor, from 1978 onward, of the base-point bookkeeping later done independently by Deligne, Ihara and Drinfeld. The technique itself is now standard, so it is of historical interest only.
missed.quote: le paquet (a_i^{ωε}) est torseur sous Γ ... τ a_i^{ω,ε} = a_i^{ω,ε'}, τ b_i^ω = b_i^ω
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck independently built the real/tangential base-point formalism underlying GT-type relations. Mathematically it adds nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine setup of equivariant base points and paths. The ideas (tangential base points, S_3 and complex-conjugation symmetry) are standard in the later literature. Its only interest is historical, as evidence of early independent development.
transcription_corrections: '(quand du tour)' in (23) should read '(quart de tour)': the arcs a_i are quarter-turns on the boundary circle U_i from S_i^ε to R_i^ω.

Top line: likely 'ω ≃ {±1}' (the '5' above appears to be a separate mark or footnote, not an exponent), followed by 'bijective ... on a donc ω ≃ ε', identifying ω with the set ε of the two hemispheres.
Margin: 'le paquet (a_i^{ωε}) est torseur sous Γ = G_J × {1,τ}' (order 12), rather than 'G_J^{1,2}'.
Margin NB: 'Rep(J) ≃ J × ω, (i,j,k) ↦ (i, ω_{ijk})' (ordering ↦ first element plus cyclic orientation).
Ensemble labels in (21): ε ∈ ε (hemispheres), not 'Σ'.
'Dec(Σ_R, J)' = Σ_R cut (découpé) at the points of J.
